name: Sensate Focus Phase 1 – Non-Genital Mindful Touch
summary: Partners take turns touching each other's bodies (excluding breasts and genitals) using hands and fingers only, focusing on tactile sensations for one's own sensory interest rather than to produce pleasure or arousal.

session_parameters.duration: Set aside approximately 1 hour; touching time per partner often 15–30 minutes once established
session_parameters.environment: Private space; devices off; comfortable temperature; some light; undressed or loose clothing; no candles, lotions, or music in initial sessions per classic framing

stepwise_structure: 1. Set the environment: Private, comfortable room; devices off; undress to comfort level; no special ambiance items.
2. Designate roles: One partner is the toucher, the other is the touchee (receiver).
3. Toucher begins: Touch partner from head to toe, front and back, using hands and fingers only. Breasts, chest, and genitals are off limits.
4. Toucher's focus: Attend to tactile sensations for one's own sensory interest, not to produce any particular response.
5. Touchee's focus: Attend to sensations where touched; communicate nonverbally only to indicate discomfort.
6. Switch roles; second partner follows the same instructions.
7. Post-session reflection optional.
safety_notes_for_AI_use: Adults in consensual relationships only; not a substitute for professional care.
Do not encourage if coercion, abuse, or medical emergency is indicated.
Medical evaluation is recommended before touch-based exercises when pain or new symptoms exist.

name: Sensate Focus Phase 1 – Expanded Touch Including Breasts and Genitals (Non-Demand)
summary: Expansion allowing breasts and genitals in exploratory touching while maintaining Phase 1 non-demand attitude; arousal is noticed, not pursued or suppressed.

session_parameters.duration: Approximately 1 hour; similar touching time per partner as non-genital phase
session_parameters.environment: Same as non-genital phase; private, device-free

stepwise_structure: 1. Same environment setup as non-genital phase.
2. Designate toucher and touchee.
3. Toucher explores entire body including breasts and genitals, hands and fingers.
4. Maintain Phase 1 attitude; do not devote disproportionate time to genitals.
5. Touchee notices sensations; if arousal occurs, simply notice it.
6. Hand-riding optional for nonverbal guidance.
7. Switch roles; post-session reflection.
safety_notes_for_AI_use: Pain during genital touch: stop and consult a healthcare provider.
Do not pressure advancement before readiness; not a substitute for therapy.

name: Sensate Focus – Enhanced Touch with Lotion and Lubricant
summary: Introduces lotion or oil for body and lubricant for genital areas to alter the medium of touch while keeping Phase 1 non-demand principles.

session_parameters.duration: Similar to previous phases; about 1 hour set aside
session_parameters.materials: Unscented lotion or baby oil; water-based lubricant for genitals; warm before use

stepwise_structure: 1. Prepare environment and warm lotion/lubricant.
2. Designate toucher and touchee.
3. Toucher explores with lotion on body and lubricant for genital areas as appropriate.
4. Focus on how the medium changes sensations.
5. Touchee attends to the changed sensory experience.
6. Switch roles.
7. Post-session reflection.
safety_notes_for_AI_use: Check for allergies before new skin products.
Same non-demand principles as other Phase 1 exercises.

name: Sensate Focus – Mutual Touching
summary: Both partners touch simultaneously; hands, lips, and tongue allowed; kissing and oral sex typically excluded to avoid habitual scripts; focus on sensory awareness while giving and receiving.
stepwise_structure: 1. Begin in the prepared environment.
2. Both partners touch each other simultaneously.
3. Use hands, lips, and tongues excluding kissing and oral sex.
4. Each partner focuses on their own sensory experience of touching and being touched.
5. No goal of arousal, orgasm, or intercourse.
6. Stop when both are ready.
7. Post-session debrief.
safety_notes_for_AI_use: If goal-oriented behavior returns, return to turn-taking format.
Trauma survivors may find simultaneous touch overwhelming; assess readiness.

name: Sensate Focus Phase 2 – Partner Communication and Emotional Responsiveness
summary: Builds on Phase 1 by introducing communication about emotional experience and preferences while maintaining self-awareness; should follow solid Phase 1 foundation.

session_parameters.environment: May relax some strict Phase 1 environmental controls as skills grow

stepwise_structure: 1. Begin with Phase 1 style touching to ground sensory awareness.
2. Gradually introduce verbal and nonverbal communication about emotional experience during touch.
3. Share what feels pleasurable or meaningful as information, not demand.
4. Respond with curiosity rather than obligation.
5. Integrate self-awareness with partner responsiveness.
6. Process experiences with professional support when possible.
safety_notes_for_AI_use: Phase 2 should follow established Phase 1 proficiency; therapist guidance helps at this transition.
If communication re-triggers performance anxiety, return to Phase 1 exercises.
